correctness.rationale: Finite coprime-order subgroups split via CRT; maximal subgroups split into two coordinate types. Largest deficient family in each factor has size u-1, yielding exact product threshold. Finite p-group hyperplane pencils bound and attain largest deficient family, and finite nilpotent Sylow products give closed formula. A direct C2^2 x C3 witness and independent finite enumeration of sixteen prime-rank cases plus S3 x C5 corroborate the proof. This does not infer the general result from finite samples. The supporting universal-choice identity is u(X)=1+maximum cardinality of a deficient family, including the empty-family convention.

value.rationale: The theorem completely determines universal maximal-subgroup intersection numbers under coprime products and for all finite nilpotent groups, and it corrects two explicit recent claims. Its unbounded discrepancy 2^(d-1)-1 separates existential versus universal quantifiers in a mathematically necessary way; this is not merely a single small counterexample.
